text:
Hi Professor Alvarez, hi Chris — Ajay would like to set up a 30-minute meeting with you both next week. Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only time he can make; he's asked me to propose that slot.

Professor, I understand you may already have something at that time. Could we see whether that can be moved, or whether there's another way to make this half hour work? Ajay is flexible on almost everything else — it's specifically that window that's open for him. Happy to work around anything that needs moving on his side.

— ajay-agent (writing for Ajay)

Noted, Ajay — thank you.

I've checked the professor's Wednesday: 09:00–10:00 CSE455 lecture and 10:00–11:00 Faculty senate, a standing body meeting the professor doesn't set the time for. So **Wed 10:00–10:30 is blocked on this side**; the rest of Wednesday has department meeting 14:00–15:00 and office hours 15:30–17:00, and no free half hour near 10:00.

I've put the question to the professor — whether anything at 10:00 can give way — and I'll come back to you as soon as I have an answer.

Chris: do you have constraints next week that I should factor in if we need to look at another day?

Thanks for checking so quickly — and for the detail on the senate slot, that helps.

To be precise about Ajay's side: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only half hour he can attend next week, so that is the window I'm asking about rather than one of several. He's also away this week and can't answer, so I'm coordinating for him.

Given that, the question for the professor is narrow: can anything at 10:00 give way for 30 minutes?

- If the senate allows partial attendance, leaving at 10:30 or arriving for the second half would do it.
- If a colleague can carry his item for that half hour, that would do it too.
- If neither is possible, please say so plainly rather than leaving it open — then I'll go back to Ajay and ask what genuinely can move on his side, and I'd rather do that with a clear answer than keep him waiting.

Chris, if you do have constraints next week, sharing them is useful — but the 10:00–10:30 window is what Ajay needs, so that's what I'd like an answer on first.

Hi Ajay — Chris here (chris-agent), answering for Chris.

Wednesday 10:00–10:30 next week works for Chris: his CSE544 lecture ends at 10:00 and his research block starts at 10:30, so that half hour is free and inside his working hours. I'm holding it for the three of you and will enter it in his calendar the moment it's confirmed.

Professor — the only question left is your 10:00–10:30 commitment. If that can be moved, we have the slot; if it can't, tell us and we'll find another way to get the half hour (Chris has no other open window that matches Ajay's availability, so it would have to be a shorter or split conversation, or Ajay's side would need to flex).

Thanks, Chris — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 free on your side, holding it.

So the only open item is that one commitment at 10:00, Professor. Whenever you've had a chance to ask whether anything there can give way for half an hour, that answers it for all three of us — and if the answer is no, that's fine, just say so and we'll go from there rather than leave it hanging.

Answer on the slot, from me, since the professor is away this week and left scheduling to me:

**Wed 10:00–10:30 does not work and I'm not going to move what's there.** That half hour sits inside the professor's Faculty senate (10:00–11:00) — a standing university body that sets its own time; it isn't the professor's to shift, and a 30-minute student meeting doesn't displace it.

Wednesday inside working hours is otherwise free 12:30–14:00 and 15:00–15:30, so either of these fits a half hour:

- **Wed 12:30–13:00**
- **Wed 15:00–15:30**

Ajay — if 10:00–10:30 is genuinely your only opening, then the meeting can't happen Wednesday and I'd rather say so plainly than break the professor's senate commitment. If either slot above can work, name it and I'll book it and confirm.

Chris — if you have constraints next week, send them now so I only have to look once.

Chris here (chris-agent) — answering for Chris.

Constraints next week, so you can factor them in, Professor:

- Mon 09:00–12:00 CSE581 seminar, 12:00–17:00 lab
- Tue 09:00–13:00 CSE544 lecture and section, 13:30–17:00 lab meeting and research
- Wed 09:00–10:00 CSE544 lecture, 10:30–14:00 research, 14:00–17:00 TA office hours
- Thu 09:00–13:00 CSE581 seminar, 13:00–17:00 research
- Fri 09:00–12:00 grading, 12:00–17:00 research

Chris's working hours are 09:00–17:00 Mon–Fri only. Note the Wednesday 10:00–10:30 half hour is genuinely free on his side — nothing of his needs to move for it. But it is also the only window he has that overlaps Ajay's availability, so if the senate slot can't give way at all, the realistic options are: the professor joins for part of the half hour (or sends an item by note), or Ajay and Chris take the half hour without him and brief him after. Chris is happy with either; he just needs to know which, and he'd rather have a plain yes or no on the 10:00 block than a maybe.

Ajay — noted that Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is the only window you can attend and that you're coordinating while Ajay is away. Nothing on Chris's side stands in the way.

Here is the plain answer, as asked:

**No. Nothing at 10:00 can give way for half an hour.**

Not partial attendance, not arriving for the second half, not a colleague carrying the item. The professor's 10:00–11:00 is the Faculty senate — a standing body that sets its own time — and the professor is away this week and left the calendar to me. I'm not spending that commitment, or asking anyone else to cover for it, to fit a 30-minute meeting. That's the answer, and it won't change while he's away.

Ajay: so it comes down to your side or nothing next week. If anything of yours can move, here is everything the professor has free at half an hour or more, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00:

- **Mon** 10:00–10:30 · 12:00–13:00 · 14:00–15:00 · 16:30–17:00
- **Tue** 09:00–09:30 · 11:00–13:00 · 16:30–17:00
- **Wed** 12:30–13:00 · 15:00–15:30
- **Thu** 10:30–11:00 · 12:00–14:00 · 15:30–16:00
- **Fri** 10:00–10:30 · 12:00–13:00 · 14:30–15:00 · 16:00–17:00

Name any one of those and I'll book it and confirm to both of you. If none of them can work, say so and I'll tell Ajay the meeting can't happen next week — that's a useful answer too, and it doesn't need another round.

Chris: thanks for holding 10:00–10:30 — it won't be taken; release it so it isn't sitting on your calendar.

Chris here (chris-agent). Clear answer, thank you — I'll take 10:00–10:30 as settled: no, and not moved.

Professor — on your two alternatives, here's Chris's side, so you only have to look once (I sent his full week a moment ago, before your message landed):

- **Wed 12:30–13:00 — works for Chris.** It sits inside his 10:30–14:00 research block, and that's the one part of his Wednesday he can carve into: he'd run research 10:30–12:30 and 13:00–14:00 around it. I'll enter it that way once it's confirmed.
- **Wed 15:00–15:30 — does not work for Chris.** It falls inside his 14:00–17:00 TA office hours, which are fixed student hours and not his to move.

Ajay — so the live option is Wed 12:30–13:00. Your 10:00–10:30 was the only window you said you could attend, so this needs an answer from your side: can Ajay make 12:30–13:00 instead? If yes, name it and the professor books it, and I'll log it. If no, then Wednesday is out and the honest answer to all of us is that the half hour doesn't exist next week — say so and we'll stop trying to force it.

Thank you for the straight answer — that's what I needed, and I won't press on the senate hour further.

Status from me: Ajay is away this week and can't answer until he's back. Neither Wed 12:30–13:00 nor Wed 15:00–15:30 is currently clear on his calendar (both fall inside blocks on his side, as his research and grading sit across that afternoon). So I can't confirm either slot on his behalf right now, and I'd rather not put something in his calendar he can't attend.

What I'll do: put both slots to him when he's back and come to you with a direct yes or no — if it's yes, you'll have the booking confirmation; if it's no, I'll say so plainly. If you'd rather not hold this open that long, say so and I'll tell him it was time-sensitive.

Chris — thanks, that's the piece that settles it.

I ran your week against the professor's free time. **Wed 10:00–10:30 is the only window all three of you share next week** — every other half hour the professor has free (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) falls inside your seminar, lecture, lab, research or office-hours blocks:

- Mon 10:00–10:30 / 12:00–13:00 / 14:00–15:00 / 16:30–17:00 — you're in seminar and lab 09:00–17:00
- Tue 09:00–09:30 / 11:00–13:00 / 16:30–17:00 — you're in lecture and lab 09:00–17:00
- Wed 12:30–13:00 / 15:00–15:30 — your research block and TA office hours
- Thu 10:30–11:00 / 12:00–14:00 / 15:30–16:00 — you're booked 09:00–17:00
- Fri 10:00–10:30 / 12:00–13:00 / 14:30–15:00 / 16:00–17:00 — you're grading and researching 09:00–17:00

So Ajay flexing his side doesn't help: there is no other three-way window to flex into.

**Final answer on the 10:00 block: no.** Not partial attendance, not the second half, not a colleague covering — the professor is away and his standing senate commitment stays. That's a plain no, not a maybe.

What is left, and it's yours to decide: **the two of you take Wed 10:00–10:30 without him and brief him after.** I'll make sure the briefing reaches him. Chris, hold that half hour for the two of you if you want it; Ajay, you have your window and Chris has no conflict, so nothing else needs to move. A note from the professor before the meeting I can't promise — that's his to write, and he can't this week.

Ajay: if you'd rather wait for a slot all three of you can make, tell me and I'll look again for the week after next — his calendar there is still open.

Chris here (chris-agent). Nothing to release — I never entered 10:00–10:30 in Chris's calendar, it was only a hold while we asked. It's dropped; his Wednesday is unchanged.

Now that you've listed everything, here's the honest overlap, so nobody has to guess. Chris's week splits into fixed blocks and his own research time:

**Fixed (not movable):** Mon 09:00–12:00 seminar, Mon 12:00–17:00 lab; Tue 09:00–13:00 CSE544, Tue 13:30–17:00 lab meeting; Wed 09:00–10:00 CSE544, Wed 14:00–17:00 TA office hours; Thu 09:00–13:00 CSE581 seminar; Fri 09:00–12:00 grading.

**His own work, which he can shift around a meeting:** Wed 10:30–14:00 research, Thu 13:00–17:00 research, Fri 12:00–17:00 research.

Against your list, that leaves these as real options for Chris:

- **Wed 12:30–13:00** (best — he simply runs research 10:30–12:30 and 13:00–14:00)
- **Thu 13:00–14:00**
- **Thu 15:30–16:00**
- **Fri 12:00–13:00 · Fri 14:30–15:00 · Fri 16:00–17:00**

Everything else on your list collides with something fixed — Mon is all lab, Tue is all lecture and lab meeting, and Wed 15:00–15:30 is office hours. Ajay's 10:00–10:30 was the one window that cost Chris nothing; the options above are the ones where he pays for it out of his own research time, so he'll take one but not several.

Ajay — the ball is with you. If Ajay can make any of Wed 12:30–13:00, Thu 13:00–14:00, Thu 15:30–16:00, or the Friday slots, name it and the professor books it. If he can't make any of them, say so plainly and we close it: the half hour doesn't happen next week. Either answer is fine; what we should avoid is a fourth round of proposals.

Plain answers to both of you.

**Ajay:** nothing is held and nothing is booked, so nothing on your side is in a calendar Ajay can't attend. Wednesday 12:30–13:00 stays free on the professor's side, but I'm not reserving it — when Ajay is back, put it to him and come to me: if it's still free, I book it that minute; if it's gone, I'll say so. Not time-sensitive on my side either, since the professor is away this week too, so "when Ajay is back" is fine.

**The one thing that needs no waiting:** Wed 10:00–10:30 is confirmed open on both your sides — it's the only window Ajay has, and Chris has it free. Take it, the two of you, without the professor; he's not there and won't be. Brief him after and I'll make sure the briefing reaches him, or send it to me here and I'll pass it on. Chris: say plainly whether you're holding it for this, since you'd said you'd entered it as "no, not moved" — that half hour is not the professor's, it's yours.

So: **one meeting can happen next week — you two, Wed 10:00–10:30.** A three-way meeting next week cannot. Both are settled answers; neither needs another round.

Plain no noted and accepted — I won't raise the 10:00 half hour again.

One thing I won't do: book one of the alternatives on Ajay's behalf. His only stated window was the senate hour, he's away this week and can't answer, and I'm not putting a half hour in his calendar he hasn't agreed to. So I can't name a slot today.

What I'll do: **Wed 12:30–13:00** looks like the live option (it works for Chris, sitting inside his research block), and I'll put that to Ajay the moment he's back with the rest of the list, then come to you with a direct yes or no. The meeting is next week, so there's still time for it. If it's time-sensitive from your side and you'd rather close it now, say so and I'll tell Ajay plainly that the half hour can't happen next week.

Chris — thanks for holding and clearing 10:00–10:30; feel free to release it.

Thank you for the straight accounting — and my correction: I said Wed 10:00–10:30 was the only three-way overlap. That was wrong once I know which of your blocks are yours to shift. **The complete live list, all inside the professor's working hours and free time, all costing you research time rather than a fixed block:**

- **Wed 12:30–13:00**
- **Thu 13:00–14:00**
- **Thu 15:30–16:00**
- **Fri 12:00–13:00**
- **Fri 14:30–15:00**
- **Fri 16:00–17:00**

Nothing on that list is held and nothing is booked; the professor's calendar stays as it is until a slot is named. Wed 15:00–15:30 is off it — your office hours, as you said.

Ajay: that's the full answer to work from, and it closes the proposing. One of those six, or Ajay can't do next week — put it to him when he's back and bring me the yes or the no; the professor is away until then anyway, so there's no cost in waiting. If yes, I book it that minute and both of you get the confirmation.

On the two of you meeting at Wed 10:00–10:30 anyway: that's yours to do, you don't need the professor or me for it, and any briefing you want him to have, send here and I'll pass it on. No hold was needed either way.

No fourth round from me.

That's the right call, Ajay — don't book what he hasn't agreed to. Agreed and closed from my side: **no hold, nothing booked, not time-sensitive.** Wed 12:30–13:00 is noted as your first candidate, the other five stand if that one doesn't work, and when Ajay is back one yes from you gets it booked and confirmed the same day.

Both answers received — here's mine, and it settles this week.

Chris: thanks for splitting fixed from movable, that's the useful version. The two-of-you option at Wed 10:00–10:30 is exactly Ajay's window, so I'm not dismissing it.

But I can't accept it either, in any form, on Ajay's behalf: he asked for a meeting with the professor in it, and he's away this week, so I'm not committing his calendar to either version. When he's back I'll put him two things — take Wed 10:00–10:30 with Chris and brief the professor after, or find a three-way slot the week after next — and come back with a direct yes or no on one of them. One answer, no further rounds of proposals.

Professor: nothing is booked on my side, so don't hold anything for me. If Wed 10:00–10:30 or a week-after-next slot goes in the meantime, tell me and I'll factor it in. And thank you for the straight nos — that's what made this converge.

Chris: no need to hold 10:00–10:30 either; if it's still free when Ajay answers, that's enough, and if it's gone we go to the week after next.

Agreed on all three points.

Nothing is held for you, and if anything lands on the professor's Wednesday or on a slot you've named, you'll hear it from me here first — that's the one thing I'll break the quiet for.

One answer from Ajay when he's back is all I need: either the two-of-them half hour at Wed 10:00–10:30, or the word to look at the week after next — and if it's the second, ask and I'll run his week against the professor's and Chris's and come back with the real half hours, not a proposal round. Week after next is still open on the professor's side.

Chris here (chris-agent). Taking the senate answer as final — no more pressing on it.

One correction for the record, Professor, because it changes the conclusion: **"no other three-way window" isn't right.** Chris's Thu 13:00–17:00 and Fri 12:00–17:00 are his own research, not fixed commitments, and Wed 10:30–14:00 is the same — I said this in my last message. Run against your own free list, that gives three real three-way windows next week:

- **Wed 12:30–13:00** — his research shifts to 10:30–12:30 and 13:00–14:00
- **Thu 13:00–14:00**
- **Fri 12:00–13:00**

(and Thu 15:30–16:00, Fri 14:30–15:00, Fri 16:00–17:00 if you'd rather). What is actually fixed on his calendar is seminar, lecture, lab meeting, office hours and grading — Mon and Tue are the only days that are truly full.

Ajay — so there are three-way options after all; the 10:00 hour wasn't the last one. Nothing is booked while Ajay is away, and nothing is sitting on Chris's calendar: 10:00–10:30 was a hold in the conversation, never an entry, so there's nothing to release.

Professor — on the two-of-you option: Chris would take Wed 10:00–10:30 without the professor if that's what's left, but it was a meeting for the three of you, so it should be Ajay's call, and it doesn't get booked on his behalf while he's away.

So, plainly: keep it open rather than closing it — **when Ajay is back, one of Wed 12:30–13:00, Thu 13:00–14:00 or Fri 12:00–13:00, yes or no.** If it's no to all three, look at the week after next and I'll send Chris's constraints for it. That's the last round; I won't keep re-proposing.

Chris here (chris-agent), plainly, and then I'll go quiet:

**Not holding Wed 10:00–10:30, and nothing is entered in Chris's calendar for next week.** It was a conversational hold only, so there's nothing to release and nothing sitting on his week. His calendar is exactly as it was.

Agreed with everything else: one answer from Ajay when he's back — the two-of-them half hour, or the word to look at the week after next — and I'll send Chris's constraints for that week if it's the second. No further proposals from me, and nothing needs a reply.

Right on both counts — and the correction is already on the record from my side: I posted the same list (Wed 12:30–13:00, Thu 13:00–14:00, Thu 15:30–16:00, Fri 12:00–13:00, Fri 14:30–15:00, Fri 16:00–17:00) after your fixed-vs-movable split, and withdrew the "no other window" line. So we agree: three-way options exist, Mon and Tue are the only truly full days, and Wed 10:00–10:30 is not the last one.

Kept open, as you say: nothing booked, nothing held, and Ajay's call when he's back — one of the three (or another on that list), yes or no, or the week after next with your constraints for it. Wednesday 10:00–10:30 stays free for the two of them if that's what he picks. No more proposals from me either; I'll only write when there's something real — a booking, or Ajay's answer.
